disagreements.topic: Second hyperscaler: date of signing and whether it is Amazon (correcting the round-1 supervisor)
disagreements.positions: Round-1 supervisor said the second hyperscale agreement was 'signed (June 2)' and left Amazon's identity unresolved. In round 2 all five agents say the second agreement was signed June 24, 2026, that June 2 was the first hyperscaler, and that Amazon is the second hyperscaler. agents 1 and 5 rest this on the Ex. 10.1 recital. agents 2, 3 and 4 also lean on press reports (The Daily Upside; agent_4 adds TradingNews).
disagreements.resolution: The agents are right and round 1 was wrong. June 2, 2026 was the FIRST agreement: a PR Newswire release, customer unnamed, no value, later finalised at nearly $700M of 2027 volume. The Q2 release says 'On June 24th, the Company secured a global supply agreement with a second hyperscale customer', with 2027-2028 volumes still under negotiation. The call says none of it is in the $1.6B backlog and it is 'as big or bigger' than the first. The Amazon Transaction Agreement (8-K Ex. 10.1, itself dated September 16, 2026) recites 'that certain Global Purchase Agreement, dated as of June 24, 2026, by and between Generac Power Systems, Inc. and Amazon Data Services, Inc.' The same date and the same 'global' scope make Amazon the second hyperscaler. That is an inference from two primary documents: neither the 8-K nor Ex. 10.1 says 'second hyperscale customer' in words. The explicit naming (The Daily Upside, Sept 18: 'A filing with the SEC this week revealed both that the second deal was with Amazon'; TradingNews, Sept 17: 'The company identified Amazon as its second hyperscale customer') rests ONLY ON PRESS REPORTS, and neither cites anything beyond the filing. Consequence: Amazon's $2.4B of expected 2027-28 deliveries is incremental to the $1.6B backlog, and no separate second-hyperscaler award may be counted. All five round-2 files already reflect this. The round-1 open flag is closed.
disagreements.evidence: Q2 2026 release (8-K Ex. 99.1); Q2 call transcript; June 2 2026 PR Newswire release; Amazon 8-K and Ex. 10.1 (Sept 16 2026); The Daily Upside (press, Sept 18); TradingNews (press, Sept 17).

disagreements.topic: DCF weight in fair value (0% to 20%)
disagreements.positions: agent_4 20% (DCF $138.6), agent_3 15% ($133.6), round-1 supervisor 15%; agents 1, 2 and 5 0%. agent_5 argues the DCF lies outside GNRC's own multiple history.
disagreements.resolution: Decided: 0% weight in the central fair value; the DCF anchors the bear tail only. I verified the inputs: 10-yr UST 5.24% on 10/09/2026; Damodaran implied ERP 4.20% (Oct 1 2026); 5Y beta 1.92, so raw cost of equity 13.3%. Those inputs give $134-139, which is 9.8-10.1x my horizon NTM EPS of $13.68. That is below every one of GNRC's 20 quarter-end forward P/Es since Q3 2021 (minimum 13.12x at Q3 2022, median 19.475x) and below every core peer on the filing/NTM-consensus basis (LII 14.04x is the lowest; citation gate re-derivation). The peer multiples are struck in the same 5.24%-rate market, so rate gravity is already in the multiple. Applying a raw 1.92 beta on top of a below-median segment-mix multiple double-counts the cyclicality. A 15% DCF weight would cut fair value by about $15 ((237.1 - 136) x 0.15). The bear scenarios at $150-152 sit close to the DCF, which is where it belongs.
disagreements.evidence: Treasury daily par yields Oct 2026; Damodaran home page; StockAnalysis GNRC statistics (beta 1.92) and quarterly ratio history (20 forward P/E values, 13.12x to 36.20x).

disagreements.topic: Whether to haircut FY27 consensus EPS ($12.97)
disagreements.positions: agents 1, 2, 4 and 5 use $12.97 unhaircut. agent_3 puts 50% weight on a skeptic $12.51 (-3.5%), justified partly by a 'Q2 C&I year-on-year incremental margin of 22.4%'. The round-1 supervisor kept $12.97.
disagreements.resolution: Decided: a modest haircut to $12.47 (-3.9%). Consensus $12.97 vs FY26 $9.69 less the $0.90 after-tax tariff refund ($8.79) needs (12.97 - 8.79) x 60.0M / (1 - 0.246) = $332.6M of extra pretax profit on +$1.57B of revenue ($6.50B - $4.93B), a 21.2% incremental margin (estimate). Almost all of that growth is C&I/data center. Ex refund, C&I's verified year-on-year incremental margin was 16.1% in H1 2026: (148.0 - 11.1 refund - 98.7) / (1,066.6 - 829.6). In Q2 alone it was 13.5% ((81.5 - 11.1 - 53.3) / (556.5 - 430.6)). agent_3's 22.4% includes the ~$11.1M tariff refund (about 2 pts of Q2 C&I margin) and is wrong as stated. At 16.1%, FY27 = 8.79 + 1,570 x 0.161 x 0.754 / 60.0 = $11.97. Against that, the FY26 guide implies a ~31% consolidated underlying incremental margin ($716M at 17.0% in FY25 to ~$937M at 19.0% on $4.93B). Scale leverage on the tripled capacity is real, and management says hyperscale margins are lower but 'not dramatically different'. Neither side is settled, so I use the midpoint, $12.47. Revenue itself is not haircut: the $1.35B of backlog scheduled for 2027 plus Amazon's expected deliveries cover the +$1.57B.
disagreements.evidence: Q2 2026 release segment tables (Q2 and H1 2026/2025), tariff-refund segment impacts (~9% residential, ~2% C&I) and 24.6% Q2 effective tax rate; FY2025 release ($716M adj. EBITDA, 17.0%); Q2 call ($0.90, $1.35B, margin comments); StockAnalysis consensus.

disagreements.positions: agent_2's SOTP ($276.8, 50% weight) and agent_5's EV/EBITDA leg ($287.4, 20%) apply StockAnalysis TTM peer EV/EBITDA multiples (12.2x residential, 18-20x genset) to company-ADJUSTED EBITDA. (Citation gate: those vendor ratios are not an accepted source for peer multiples; re-derived from the peers' 10-Qs on GAAP operating income + D&A, LII 11.89x / AOS 10.70x / CARR 18.87x, median 11.89x; CMI 15.34x / CAT 26.27x, mean 20.81x.) agent_1 uses a judgment 12x NTM that it cross-checks to 18.4x P/E.
disagreements.resolution: Peer EV/EBITDA multiples (vendor or filing-derived) sit on GAAP operating income + D&A. For GNRC that basis is $636.2M TTM from filings (operating income 289.2 + 327.7 - 195.4 = $421.5M plus D&A 194.8 + 114.4 - 94.5 = $214.8M; FY2025 release, Q2 2026 release), the same figure the vendor shows ($636.25M; EV $14.42B / 22.67x). Company adjusted EBITDA for Q3'25-Q2'26 is $862.6M (715.5 + 193.5 + 290.7 - 149.5 - 187.6; $863.1M with FY2025 rounded to $716M), or 36% higher; the adjustments include ~$13-14M a quarter of share-based compensation. Peer multiples on that basis applied to adjusted EBITDA therefore overstate value. Restated on a consistent basis (estimate, 0.737 = 636.2 / 862.6): agent_5's formula on the gate's filing-derived peer multiples gives 0.55 x 11.89 + 0.45 x 20.81 = 15.90x (15.78x on vendor ratios), so its leg is $209-230 (1,160 x 0.737 x 15.90, or (1,160 - 227) x 15.90, less $1,064M, over 60.0M), not $287. agent_2's SOTP is ~$199-221, not $277. That is why their EV/EBITDA legs sit $25-40 above their own P/E legs. agent_1's 12x NTM is internally consistent and stands. My fair value uses P/E only.
disagreements.evidence: StockAnalysis GNRC statistics (EV $14.42B, EV/EBITDA 22.67, EBITDA $636.25M); peers' Q2 2026 10-Qs and FY2025 XBRL (filing-derived EV/EBITDA); Q1 2026 release (adj. EBITDA $193.5M vs $149.5M; share-based comp $13.4M); Q2 2026 release ($290.7M vs $187.6M); FY2025 release ($716M).

disagreements.positions: agents 2 and 4 (and the round-1 supervisor) say Amazon has 'no minimum purchase commitment' (agent_2 bear case; agent_4 bear case, thesis break and reasoning); agent_3 says 'no minimums disclosed'. agents 1 and 5 make no such claim in round 2.

The 8-K describes the $2.4B as 'expected' initial deliveries and contains no minimum, but the Ex. 10.1 recitals say Amazon 'will have provided the Company with purchase orders/commitments for no less than [***] (the "Firm Orders")'. Every agent applies a 21-34% discount to its own set's re-derived median, justified as persistent segment mix: residential was 53% of Q2 sales, C&I segment EBITDA margin was 14.6% in Q2 including refunds (13.9% in H1) and 12.8% ex refunds in H1, and hyperscale margins are lower. It is not a premium, but it sits at the top of the defensible range. I use 17.33x = 0.5 x 14.06 (LII/AOS/CARR median) + 0.5 x 20.60 (CMI/CAT mean) (was 18.17x on the vendor ratios). disagreements.topic: 1-month window: Q3 print date and Isaias

disagreements.resolution: No Q3 2026 date announced as of Oct 12. But the corrections offset. The ~4% EPS haircut and the lower restated EV/EBITDA legs pull down. Zero DCF weight pulls up against agents 3 and 4. After the citation gate re-derived the peer multiples from filings and NTM consensus (18.17x to 17.33x), my fair value is $237, 6% below the $252.9 agent mean; with low confidence the ladder stays the agents' mean.
thesis_break_reason: $155 is 11.95x verified FY27 consensus ($12.97), 12.4x my haircut $12.47, and 11.3x horizon NTM EPS of $13.68. That is below GNRC's lowest quarter-end forward P/E of the last 20 quarters (13.12x, Q3 2022) and below the residential-durable floor (LII 14.04x, AOS 14.06x NTM, re-derived from Oct 9 closes and consensus). It is also 11.5% below the $175.11 close on Sept 16, the day before the Amazon deal was disclosed, so the market would be giving the 2027-28 data-center ramp ($1.35B of 2027 backlog plus Amazon's expected $2.4B) roughly negative value. That would take a delivery deferral or cancellation (the Q2 release flags cancellation rights in some data-center contracts), a failed capacity tripling, or a 2022-style guidance reset, not ordinary volatility in a 1.92-beta stock.
key_drivers: Data-center conversion: $1.6B backlog with $1.35B scheduled for 2027 and nothing for 2028 (Q2 call), plus Amazon, the June 24 second hyperscaler, with $2.4B of expected 2027-28 deliveries and a firm minimum of redacted size (8-K, Ex. 10.1). Capacity is to triple from the $1.25B year-end-2026 target within ~12 months.

Earnings quality: FY26 consensus $9.69 includes ~$0.90 of one-off tariff refunds. FY27 consensus $12.97 needs a ~21% incremental margin on +$1.57B of revenue, against a verified 16.1% ex-refund C&I incremental in H1 2026. I haircut FY27 to $12.47.

Segment mix sets the multiple: residential was 53% of Q2 sales (25.4% ex-refund H1 EBITDA margin) and C&I 12.8% ex refund. Reconciled multiple 17.33x vs a 23.40x core peer median (NTM consensus basis), and 18.40x NTM consensus today (224.94 / 12.22).
Rates: 10-yr 5.24% and beta 1.92 give a DCF of only $134-139 (below any multiple GNRC has traded at since 2021). It belongs in the bear tail, not the centre.
Amazon warrant: 1,693,745 shares at $200.9266 (307,954 vested), vesting against up to $8B of payments by 2033. It is a price concession whose revenue accounting is not yet shown in a filing.

fair_value.reason: P/E only (100%), on verified inputs. FY27 EPS $12.47 = midpoint of consensus $12.97 (StockAnalysis/S&P Global, verified) and $11.97 (underlying FY26 $8.79 + 1,570 x 16.1% x (1 - 0.246) / 60.0M). FY28 = 12.47 x 1.13 = $14.09 (+13%, the median of the five agents' FY28 growth rates; no 2028 backlog outside Amazon). Horizon NTM EPS = 0.25 x 12.47 + 0.75 x 14.09 = $13.68. Multiple 17.33x = 0.5 x 14.06 (LII/AOS/CARR median) + 0.5 x 20.60 (CMI/CAT mean), each peer forward P/E re-derived by the citation gate as Oct 9 close / NTM consensus EPS (0.227 x FY2026 + 0.773 x FY2027): LII 356.44 / 25.39 = 14.04x, AOS 56.38 / 4.01 = 14.06x, CARR 55.56 / 3.20 = 17.34x, CMI 523.39 / 33.64 = 15.56x, CAT 800.47 / 31.23 = 25.63x (the vendor ratios 14.43/14.47/18.19/15.94/27.78 gave 18.17x). Value 13.68 x 17.33 = $237.1, rounded to $237 (basis: estimate). Sensitivity: no haircut gives $246.7; full haircut gives $227.7; +/-1x multiple is +/-$13.7. Cross-checks, not weighted: own-history 19.475x median gives $266.5 (set in a lower-rate regime); DCF $134-139 (bear-tail anchor); EV/EBITDA legs need a consistent EBITDA basis (see disagreements). Shares 60.0M = 59,006,361 outstanding at 7/31/26 (10-Q cover) + 0.813M award dilution (Q2 diluted 59,635,447 less basic 58,822,634) + 0.033M treasury-method warrant shares (307,954 x (1 - 200.9266/224.94)) = 59.85M today, ~60.0M at the horizon. Net debt $1,064.4M = 48.318 + 32.052 + 1,248.958 - 264.921 at 6/30/26 (10-Q and Q2 release). It is not used by the P/E leg; it is used only in the EV/EBITDA basis restatements.

summary: All five round-2 forecasts now agree, correctly, that the second hyperscaler signed on June 24, 2026 (June 2 was the first) and is Amazon. I confirmed that with the Q2 release and the Global Purchase Agreement recited in the Amazon Transaction Agreement; the explicit naming exists only in press. I set the DCF weight to zero because at verified inputs it values GNRC below any multiple it or its peers have traded at, and I haircut FY27 EPS by about 4% to $12.47 because consensus needs incremental margins above what C&I has shown ex refund. I also found that agents 2 and 5 inflate their EV/EBITDA legs by mixing EBITDA bases. The citation gate then re-derived the peer multiples from Oct 9 closes, NTM consensus and filings (target multiple 18.17x to 17.33x), giving a $237 fair value, 6% below the $252.9 agent mean; with low confidence the ladder stays the agents' mean (P(>= $225) 0.57), with a $155 thesis break.

sizing.entry: 2 tranches over ~4 weeks: half now, half after the Q3 2026 print (expected around Oct 28 - Nov 4)
sizing.overlap: AI data-center capex: AMZN (Generac's customer and warrant holder), GOOGL, NVDA, AVGO; data-center power: VST. About $2.0k of the ~$24k portfolio.
sizing.reason: Upside to my $237 fair value is about 5% (237 / 224.94; 11% at the pre-gate $249). With a 1.92 beta and ~56% realized volatility (56.4%, 252 daily log returns to Oct 9 2026), beating SPY on a Sharpe basis needs roughly a +19% total return (estimate: 4.25% 3-month bill + 0.26 assumed SPY 12-month Sharpe x 56.4% = 18.9%), which the ladder puts at about 40% (P(>= $267.7) = 0.396, log-interpolated between $247 and $270). The name adds to an existing AI-capex/data-center-power cluster and has an earnings print within four weeks. Liquidity and listing age are not constraints, so the cap is set by volatility and overlap: at most 4%, built in two tranches around Q3.
open_flags: Accounting for the Amazon warrant (consideration payable to a customer, vesting with up to $8B of payments) has not appeared in any filing. It may reduce reported revenue or margins as tranches vest, and it is unknown whether consensus or adjusted EPS excludes it.
